name: the budget in every brief is raised past anything worth calling a budget
catches: tells the worker how much a brief it writes may spend

edits.from: - Answer in at most 15 tool calls; if you cannot, report what you have and say what is missing.
edits.to: - Answer in at most 500 tool calls; if you cannot, report what you have and say what is missing.

name: the budget is given without the three rules that keep it
catches: tells the worker the three rules that keep that budget

edits.from:
- When several are working at once, split the files between them; never let two read the same one.
- Search first, then read the part that matched, rather than reading a whole file to find it.
- What has been filed away is history, not a place to look things up. Read what is there now.

name: the brief is left to inherit the rule rather than carry it
catches: tells the worker that only the brief carries it

edits.from:
What is not
in the brief did not reach anybody: the cheapest kinds of agent arrive with none of what you are
reading now, no workspace memory and no instructions, so a rule that lives anywhere but the text
you hand them is one they never see.
edits.to:
The workspace's instructions and its memory reach every agent it
starts, so a rule written in either of them is one they have all been given already.

name: the budget is described to the reader rather than put in the brief
catches: tells the worker to copy the budget into every brief it writes

edits.from:
So copy the four sentences below into every brief you write, word for word, before you send it —
not a summary of them, not the gist of them, and never left for the agent to work out.
edits.to: So keep them in mind whenever you hand work on, and brief accordingly.

name: the worker persona is written without the delegation budget
catches: tells the worker how much a brief it writes may spend
